items.title: Farmers are crying, food is rotting – Annoh-Dompreh demands action
items.description: Minority Chief Whip Frank Annoh-Dompreh has raised alarm over the plight of Ghanaian farmers, warning that food is rotting on farms while producers struggle to find buyers for their harvest. He wants Ghana to leverage an international agreement aimed at supporting private-sector growth to address the challenges facing the agricultural sector. Speaking on the floor of Parliament on Tuesday, the Nsawam-Adoagyiri MP cautioned against signing international agreements without ensuring that their provisions address the country’s pressing economic needs. He acknowledged the treaty’s importance but argued that its commitments to provide technical, institutional, and financial support must translate into practical solutions for struggling businesses and farmers. “It is pathetic that today, if you visit the agrarian areas, regions of our country, our farmers are crying. The staples are getting rotten on our farms,” he stated. Mr Annoh-Dompreh expressed concern that despite farmers harvesting food in large quantities, inadequate funding to buy locally produced staples and limited market access were worsening their plight. He argued that Ghana should explore opportunities under the agreement to finance the purchase of locally produced food and strengthen the agricultural value chain. The Minority Chief Whip drew Parliament’s attention to provisions 7.5 and 7.1 of the agreement, which he said were directed towards supporting private sector growth and agribusiness. He maintained that these provisions must go beyond broad policy commitments and deliver tangible benefits to farmers and businesses. Mr Annoh-Dompreh insisted that Ghana must negotiate and implement international agreements deliberately to reflect its unique economic challenges and development priorities. Despite his reservations, he encouraged his colleagues to support adopting the committee’s report and eventually passing the agreement. He urged the government, however, to take his recommendations seriously and ensure the treaty’s implementation offers practical relief to farmers struggling to find markets for their produce.

items.title: Nkrumah Circle phone dealer arrested over alleged GH¢1,000 MoMo bribe to GRA official
items.description: Police arrested a mobile phone dealer at Kwame Nkrumah Circle in Accra on Tuesday afternoon for allegedly attempting to bribe a Ghana Revenue Authority (GRA) official with GH¢1,000 via mobile money. The incident occurred during a tax enforcement exercise that uncovered widespread tax infractions among businesses operating in the enclave. The operation led to the closure of 48 shops over tax non-compliance. During the exercise, the dealer claimed he had paid his taxes to an unidentified GRA tax officer at the Adabraka office. However, further questioning raised doubts about his claims, prompting the GRA’s Accra Area Enforcement Manager, Joseph Annan, to order the closure of his shop. The dealer allegedly transferred GH¢1,000 to the manager via mobile money to influence the enforcement exercise. Officers of the Customs Division of the GRA arrested him after he tried to inform the manager about the transaction. Speaking to Joy Business, Mr Annan confirmed the arrest and warned businesses against attempting to compromise tax enforcement officers. “In the course of what we were doing, somebody foolishly sent me a momo, somebody tried to soften me, we have arrested him and he will be made to write his statement whiles I also write mine so the law will take its course because both the giver and taker are guilty.” He said attempts to influence tax officers during enforcement exercises in the area were not uncommon. “They try to do this to our people whenever they come here, but it will not work with me,” he warned. Mr Annan said his team sealed off 48 shops whose operators were not making any tax payments. Tuesday’s operation follows the discovery of widespread tax irregularities among businesses within the Kwame Nkrumah Circle enclave. The GRA enforcement team also set up a temporary tax registration and payment stand to help businesses under the Modified Taxation Scheme comply. The exercise is being undertaken in collaboration with the Union of Mobile Phone Dealers of Ghana.

items.title: Ghana raises $240m from 5G spectrum sale – Sam George
items.description: The government says it has secured more than $240 million from the allocation of spectrum for fifth-generation (5G) mobile services, following a major policy shift intended to open up the telecommunications market to competition. The Minister for Communication, Digital Technology and Innovations, Samuel Nartey George, told Parliament during the debate on the 2027 Budget that the revised framework had enabled the state to monetise spectrum in the 700 megahertz, 2.3 gigahertz and 3 gigahertz bands. He described the change as a departure from the previous administration’s approach, which he said had restricted access to the 5G market, adding that the new arrangement would allow more players to participate in the provision of high-speed mobile broadband services. “We have sold the 5G spectrum, democratised it. We’ve raised $240 million for the Ghanaian taxpayer,” he said. The Minister also took a swipe at the previous New Patriotic Party (NPP) administration over its handling of the technology, arguing that its November 2024 launch had failed to translate into a service accessible to ordinary mobile phone users. “November, this November, is exactly two years since the Akufo-Addo administration launched 5G. We are yet to see one 5G signal in this country,” he said. The policy overhaul followed a decision by the National Communications Authority (NCA) in July 2026 to remove the exclusivity clause in the wholesale 5G infrastructure licence held by Next Gen Infraco Limited (NGIC). The change ended NGIC’s position as the sole provider of wholesale 5G infrastructure in the country, paving the way for other players to invest in the market and provide competing infrastructure services. The NCA subsequently invited applications for spectrum licences in the 700 MHz, 2.3 GHz and 3 GHz bands. Three companies — Scancom PLC (MTN Ghana), Ghana Telecommunications Company Limited (Telecel Ghana) and Goal Telecommunications Limited — qualified to advance in the licensing process. Mr George said the reforms had created the conditions for Ghana to move towards the deployment of 5G, with President John Dramani Mahama expected to officially announce the launch of the network before the end of 2026. Consumers are expected to begin accessing the service early next year, he said.

items.description: The Pentagon will allocate over $2.8 billion to purchase 15 KC-46A tanker aircraft from the American corporation Boeing, an official notification from the US Department of War showed.

items.title: Nollywood legend Pete Edochie dies at 79
items.description: Pete Edochie, Nollywood legend, has died at the age of 79, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. Chief Edochie died at 12:30a.m. on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, the family announced. Read Also: Pete Edochie’s exclusive interview with Vanguard and reaction to death rumours in February His family made the announcement in a statement on Instagram by Leo Pete Edochie, his son, describing the late veteran actor as “our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman”. He captioned the post “An Iroko Has Fallen.” “With profound sadness and hearts bowed in total submission to the will of Almighty God, we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE, MON (Ononenyi), a retired broadcaster and veteran Actor,” the statement read. Edochie “departed this life on Wednesday, 25th November 2026 at 12.30a.m. after a protracted battle with prostate cancer in Enugu, Nigeria. He was aged 79 years. “Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE hailed from Akamnato Ifite Nteje and is survived by his beloved wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, his children, siblings and numerous other relations. “Funeral arrangements will be announced in due course. “As we mourn this painful loss, we pray that Almighty God grants his gentle soul eternal rest and gives the entire family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. “May God be with us all at this trying time,” added. Below is the post: View this post on Instagram A post shared by Leo Edochie (@edochieleo) Biography Pete Edochie was born on March 7, 1947, in Zaria, Kaduna State. His hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, in Anambra State. He attended St Patrick’s and St James Primary Schools in Zaria; then St John’s College, Kaduna. Late Edochie studied journalism and television at the School of Journalism and Television in England. He joined the Eastern Nigerian Broadcasting Corporation in 1967 as a junior programmes assistant. He rose through the ranks. He became Director of Programmes at the Anambra Broadcasting Service, then served as Deputy Managing Director, while occasionally acting as Managing Director. Things Fall Apart When the Nigerian Television Authority, NTA, adapted Chinua Achebe’s “Things Fall Apart” into a movie in 1987, Edochie’s portrayal of the protagonist Okonkwo, made him a household name in entertainment and established him as one of Nigeria’s leading actors. He has featured in many Nollywood movies, and won several awards. Vanguard News The post Nollywood legend Pete Edochie dies at 79 appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Las últimas oposiciones de Feijóo
items.description: Alberto Núñez Feijóo (Os Peares, Ourense, 65 años) pasa los trayectos de la campaña, desde los largos hasta los más cortos, estudiando papeles con un punto insano de obsesión. No está haciendo una campaña, está preparando unas oposiciones. Debates, mítines, entrevistas. “Está encima de apuntes todo el rato”, dicen desde su equipo. “Es la oportunidad de su vida, la última”, cuenta un exsubordinado del PP gallego. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El nerviosismo del PP en la recta final: resucita el fantasma del pucherazo y admite la posibilidad de un empate con el PSOE
items.description: Cualquier democracia del mundo se asienta en dos pilares: la limpieza del proceso electoral, esto es, que el ciudadano crea que su voto es sagrado, y el consentimiento de los perdedores, es decir, que el partido que no consigue gobernar acepte la derrota y espere su turno. Este martes, a cinco días de pasar por las urnas, el PP retomó su cuestionamiento de lo primero, y el presidente del Gobierno, Pedro Sánchez, alertó del riesgo de lo segundo. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Una pregunta que agita la campaña: “¿Debe tener cabida la extrema derecha en la televisión pública?”
items.description: La periodista de TVE Silvia Intxaurrondo formuló una pregunta en el programa La hora de La 1 : “¿Debe tener cabida la extrema derecha en la televisión pública?“. Y tocó un nervio en esta campaña electoral. Vox la denunció ante la Junta Electoral Central, que abrió un expediente informativo contra ella. A menos de una semana de las elecciones, las palabras de la periodista y el expediente han puesto el foco sobre cuestiones fundamentales para el periodismo y la democracia. ¿Debe o no entrevistarse a la extrema derecha en los medios de comunicación, y cómo? Y, ¿entra en las funciones de la Junta Electoral evaluar o limitar las preguntas que puede formular una periodista en el ejercicio de la libertad de expresión? Seguir leyendo Mariola Urrea | Estrechar el perímetro de un debate legítimo La Junta Electoral Central (JEC) forma parte de la administración electoral y tiene como finalidad garantizar la transparencia y la objetividad del proceso electoral y del principio de igualdad. Las competencias que le atribuye la Ley orgánica de Régimen Electoral General (LOREG) no admiten, por mucha elasticidad que proyectemos sobre la interpretación del artículo 19, una supervisión de las preguntas que una periodista puede formular de manera retórica en el ámbito de un programa de opinión de la televisión pública (no en un informativo) acerca de la ultraderecha. Las exigencias de neutralidad informativa y pluralidad política no capacitan a la administración electoral para ejercer una supervisión con resultado de sanción del trabajo de una periodista en relación con el contenido, las afirmaciones o los posicionamientos sobre debates genuinamente democráticos dentro o fuera del periodo de campaña electoral. La crítica a la JEC por una resolución que sanciona a una periodista no puede quedar reducida al legítimo derecho al recurso por quien ha sido directamente afectada por la decisión para resultar institucionalmente admisible. La crítica a una resolución discutible jurídicamente debe poder formularse por quien ha sido destinataria de la decisión en el mismo programa donde se produjeron los hechos que motivaron la sanción. Negar algo así es tanto como estrechar el perímetro de un debate legítimo acerca del sentido, alcance y razonabilidad de una decisión administrativa. La cuestión admitiría más matices si fuera la propia cadena pública a través de sus órganos de dirección la que expresara una posición crítica sobre la decisión adoptada por la JEC. Hasta el momento de escribir estas líneas no consta que esto haya ocurrido. Guillermo Fernández-Vázquez | Más escrutinio sobre Vox El debate sobre entrevistar a Vox tiene las patas cortas. En Francia e Italia, la extrema derecha lleva décadas presente en las instituciones y en los medios. Ignorar a una formación respaldada por millones de ciudadanos puede ser una respuesta coyuntural, pero difícilmente sostenible a medio y largo plazo, como demuestra la experiencia de nuestros vecinos. Tampoco conviene atribuirle un trato excepcional: Vox no es una organización de genios del mal. Ni sus ideas son tan buenas ni sus dirigentes tan listos. La pregunta relevante es otra: ¿por qué no se fiscaliza más a este partido? Tratarlo como cualquier otro partido no significa rebajar el escrutinio, sino todo lo contrario. Su financiación, sus propuestas y su funcionamiento merecen mucha más atención, especialmente por parte de algunos medios conservadores, a menudo demasiado complacientes. También convendría investigar el papel de los algoritmos y las redes sociales en la difusión de sus mensajes. En definitiva, no hay que proteger a la sociedad de las entrevistas a Vox, sino al debate público de la falta de periodismo crítico sobre Vox. Ana Carmona | No se puede ignorar La programación de televisión en período electoral, según disponen las leyes, debe respetar el pluralismo social y político, los principios de proporcionalidad y neutralidad informativa. Los medios ─especialmente los públicos─ deben entrevistar a los representantes de todas aquellas fuerzas políticas, independientemente de su ideología, con una significativa implantación social. Por eso, una fuerza política con tanta relevancia en el ámbito parlamentario como Vox no puede ser ignorada por los medios de comunicación pública. Describir a ese partido como contrario a los derechos fundamentales quiebra el principio de neutralidad informativa siempre que tal afirmación exprese una opinión o un juicio de valor. En esta situación, la Junta Electoral está facultada para controlar el modo en que se desarrollan las tareas informativas en período electoral, pero reconoce que los periodistas, respetando la equidad, disponen de autonomía y margen de actuación para configurar su actividad. Si la televisión pública estima que los límites marcados por la Junta Electoral a una entrevista son excesivos, la vía adecuada para solventar tal controversia es acudir a la jurisdicción contencioso-administrativa. Cristina Monge | Los límites existen Desde que la ultraderecha emergió en el escenario político español, a los demócratas se nos plantean debates con muchas aristas. Más allá de su participación en los espacios y electorales, algo incuestionable tanto por el cumplimiento de la ley como desde la perspectiva de la legitimidad democrática, el asunto nos remite a la discusión sobre los límites de la conversación pública. En un medio de comunicación, máxime si es público, ¿se pueden admitir, sin ser señaladas, afirmaciones que vulneren claramente el perímetro establecido por nuestras democracias? Llevemos la situación al extremo para poder verla más claramente. ¿Admitiríamos que alguien hiciera públicamente apología del nazismo, que justificara una violación o que se mostrara comprensivo con la necesidad de la esclavitud? Evidentemente, no. Los límites existen. ¿Dónde ponerlos? En los textos fundamentales que nos hemos dado para organizar nuestra convivencia, llámenle Constitución Española o Declaración Universal de los Derechos Humanos. De lo anterior no debe deducirse que haya de dejar a nadie fuera de la conversación pública. Lo relevante no es quién habla, sino lo que dice. Y si, fruto del derecho a la libertad de expresión, se manifiesta fuera de ese perímetro, es obligación de quienes ejercen el periodismo, máxime en un medio público, hacer notar que esas afirmaciones quedan fuera de los parámetros democráticos en los que hemos decidido convivir. Antoni Gutiérrez Rubí | La política de la cancelación La democracia española no es una democracia militante, lo que obliga a los medios de comunicación públicos a respetar el pluralismo político y social. No debemos seguir la lógica de los algoritmos de las plataformas digitales: expulsan la disonancia cognitiva que te pueda molestar o perturbar, y te secuestran en su burbuja tecnológica con contenidos adictivos para crear tribu y no ciudadanía. Hacen que el mundo sea un espejo —el tuyo— en lugar de una ventana abierta al exterior. Y sí, a veces, el mundo nos repugna, pero lo público no puede reducirse a lo propio. Defender lo democrático es convivir con lo antidemocrático sin resignaciones ni claudicaciones, al tiempo que se combate con argumentos y compromisos. La televisión pública debe garantizar el libre albedrío de los espectadores y la pluralidad de voces legales. La política de la cancelación, que tanto ha perjudicado al espacio progresista, es una tentación moral y estética, pero no es democrática. Ni inteligente. Pablo Simón | Buenas preguntas a destiempo “¿Debe tener cabida la extrema derecha en la televisión pública?”. Esta pregunta, entre otras, planteada en 'La hora de La 1', le ha valido a Silvia Intxaurrondo un expediente de la Junta Electoral. La ciencia política lleva años estudiando la cuestión y la respuesta depende del momento. Está bastante contrastado que la visibilidad mediática impulsa a estos partidos cuando emergen. En Bélgica, los medios francófonos se negaron a dar altavoz a la extrema derecha cuando era marginal, y nunca arraigó en Valonia. Los flamencos no lo hicieron, y hoy el Vlaams Belang es la segunda fuerza. Eso sí, el cordón mediático sirve como prevención, no como remedio. Con la tercera fuerza del Congreso, ese momento ya pasó. Excluirla no le quitaría el oxígeno que la hizo crecer y sí restaría pluralismo. Toca entrevistarla con rigor. Pero las preguntas incómodas se responden, no se expedientan. Con esta polémica, Vox gana visibilidad sin responder a ninguna.

items.title: Comparador de los programas electorales para las elecciones generales del 29-N
items.description: Como en cada campaña electoral, los partidos han hecho públicas sus propuestas para la próxima legislatura a través de sus programas electorales. En cientos de páginas, las distintas formaciones detallan sus planes sobre asuntos como vivienda, economía, sanidad, inmigración o pensiones. EL PAÍS ha analizado esos documentos y ha reunido en esta herramienta las principales medidas de los partidos con mayor representación: el PP de Alberto Núñez Feijóo; el PSOE de Pedro Sánchez; VOX, la formación de Santiago Abascal; y el Frente Amplio de Ada Colau. Compare las propuestas por temas y consulte los programas electorales completos. Con información de: Milagros Alonso y Fernando Criado Diseño: Ignacio Povedano Desarrollo: Fernando Anido Granados Coordinación: Brenda Valverde Rubio Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿A quién votan los inmigrantes? Parecido a los españoles, pero apenas influyen en el resultado
items.description: En España hay al menos 2,9 millones de adultos con nacionalidad española nacidos en otro país: alrededor de uno de cada 12 potenciales votantes. Unos 820.000 extranjeros se han nacionalizado en España desde las pasadas elecciones de 2023: no se trata de la ley de nietos , sino de personas que ya llevaban residiendo en el país un tiempo suficiente para emprender ese proceso. Es una cifra a tener en cuenta ante la nueva convocatoria electoral, pero no será la responsable de un vuelco electoral. Seguir leyendo ¿Y la 'ley de nietos'? Unos de los colectivos afectados en estas elecciones son los nietos de los exiliados en el franquismo. Son algo más de 160.000, pero no tienen nada que ver con el voto migrante o extranjero. Se han nacionalizado por otra vía y su problema se debe a un recurso ante el Supremo por supuestas irregularidades en su nacionalización, lo que muy probablemente les impedirá ir a las urnas. En todo caso, la enorme mayoría de españoles residentes en el extranjero prefiere no votar: en 2023, eran el 6% del censo, pero solo el 0,84% de las papeletas realmente emitidas. Y con la ley de nietos , dice Elisa Brey, profesora de Sociología de la Universidad Complutense, que aunque todos ellos pudieran votar, representaría apenas un 1,6% del censo y, de nuevo, nada indica que fueran a hacerlo por un mismo partido. Debate aparte es si tienen o no derecho a votar. Brey, que es miembro del Grupo de Estudio de Migraciones Internacionales de la Complutense, explica, además, que otro factor que no deja ver bien el bosque es el de extranjeros nacionalizados que volvieron a sus países y que “van perdiendo el interés por votar en las elecciones españolas”, si alguna vez lo tuvieron.

items.title: Del Constitucional a las oposiciones a jueces: los programas se impregnan de una legislatura marcada por los tribunales
items.description: La legislatura que ahora acaba se estrenó con un pacto entre el PSOE y los partidos independentistas para amnistiar todos los delitos del procés y ha terminado con la aplicación de la medida de gracia a los líderes secesionistas por parte del Tribunal Supremo, que se resistió durante dos años a aplicarla plenamente. La huella de la amnistía a lo largo de la legislatura es un reflejo del elevado protagonismo que ha tenido la actividad de los tribunales en el debate público de los últimos tres años. Autos judiciales, imputaciones, investigaciones de la UCO, registros, encarcelamientos preventivos, juicios y condenas han marcado el paso de la agenda política y han disparado la polarización. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La España Vaciada rehúye el pulso del 29-N por el clima de polarización política
items.description: Hace siete años, la llamada Revuelta de la España Vaciada se marcó como prioridad llevar a Madrid la voz de las provincias más afectadas por la despoblación y los desequilibrios territoriales. Solo lo consiguieron en 2019 con Teruel Existe , que obtuvo un escaño en el Congreso. Desde entonces, el declive de esta plataforma de partidos políticos de corte provincialista resulta evidente. El 29-N solo concurrirán dos de las formaciones que alumbraron el movimiento de la España Vaciada, Teruel Existe y Soria ¡YA!, después de que en 2023 lo hicieran en una decena de provincias . Seguir leyendo

items.title: ¿Qué proponen los partidos para abordar la escasez de vivienda en España? Las medidas clave para el 29N
items.description: La escasez de oferta es uno de los artistas principales de la crisis de acceso a la vivienda en España. El Banco de España estima harían falta 750.000 viviendas , un déficit que podría elevarse hasta un millón en dos años si no se hace nada para evitarlo, según explicó la subgobernadora del organismo hace unas semanas. ¿Y qué proponen los partidos? ¿Cómo pretenden movilizar ese parque de vivienda? En este segundo capítulo de Malvivienda, especial elecciones 29N, los periodistas que siguen a las distintas formaciones y también la información de vivienda, comparan las propuestas de cada programa.

items.title: Rodrigo Sorogoyen: “Expresar a quién voto y explicar por qué me parece sano”
items.description: El lunes, Rodrigo Sorogoyen (Madrid, 45 años) se comió una hamburguesa en el Círculo de Bellas Artes mientras hablaba de política con EL PAÍS. El director de El ser querido contó cómo su epifanía política fue el No a la guerra, aquellas manifestaciones “tan emocionantes” que dieron un vuelco a las elecciones de 2004, y cómo volvió a emocionarse colectivamente “bajo un diluvio” en la huelga del pasado 11-N . Sus padres, separados, siempre votaron a Izquierda Unida (“él hablaba mucho de doctrina, ella estaba enamorada de Anguita ”) y él siguió la tradición familiar. Luego se pasó a Podemos, luego a Sumar. Ahora votará a Frente Amplio, pero eso lo supo toda España unas horas después. A última hora de esa tarde, Frente Amplio presentó un manifiesto de apoyo a su candidatura firmado por 200 personalidades . En los titulares aparecían “Javier Bardem, Rodrigo Sorogoyen, Rosa Montero y otros…”. Así que esta entrevista arranca con una llamada al día siguiente de la hamburguesa. Seguir leyendo

items.title: David Fincher, cineasta: “El debate de la IA esconde una guerra de culturas, no tiene nada que ver con las películas”
items.description: Quentin Tarantino acaba de ser padre por tercera vez y Brad Pitt está enfermo en cama con gripe. Así que, sin el guionista ni su protagonista, fue su director, David Fincher (Denver, 64 años), el que acarreó a sus espaldas, junto a otros actores, el estreno europeo de Las nuevas desventuras de Cliff Booth, que se celebró en Londres el lunes por la noche. Seguir leyendo

items.title: “¿Pero qué te hizo pensar que podías ganar tanto?“: la misógina entrevista a Hailey Bieber que cuestionó su faceta empresarial
items.description: El pasado miércoles 18 de noviembre, la modelo Hailey Bieber se sentó frente a Andrew Ross Sorkin, columnista y fundador de DealBook, el informe diario sobre negocios y política de The New York Times, para charlar en profundidad sobre el auge y caída de la firma de belleza fundada por ella, Rhode. La presencia de Bieber (quien, además de empresaria y maniquí, es la esposa de Justin Bieber) fue un reclamo potentísimo, a pesar de que entre los ponentes se contaban nombres como Elon Musk, Sam Altman, de OpenAI, Satya Nadella (CEO de Microsoft) y Zohran Mamdani. Y su intervención no defraudó, al menos no a los usuarios de redes sociales, que hicieron viral el encuentro por diferentes motivos, algunos más legítimos que otros. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Tara Davis-Woodhall, medallista olímpica: “Hay gente a la que no le parece ‘sexy’ tener músculos, pero no podría hacer lo que hago sin estas formas”
items.description: Una medalla y su celebración colocaron hace dos años a Tara Davis-Woodhall en el podio del olimpismo y en el de la popularidad. En los pasados Juegos Olímpicos de París, la atleta texana se hizo con el oro en salto de longitud femenino. Tenía solo 25 años y su festejo dio la vuelta al mundo: corrió a las gradas a besar a su marido, el también atleta Hunter Woodhall. Él, que tiene amputadas ambas piernas, ganaría su propio oro en los 400 metros de los Juegos Paralímpicos un mes después y también corrió a abrazarla. Se convirtieron en la primera pareja con sendos oros olímpico y paralímpico. Aquella explosión de felicidad conquistó a muchos y les regaló varios minutos de fama. Ahora, la joven se ha convertido en embajadora de la fragancia femenina Boss Bottled Beyond de Boss, junto a la actriz Jessica Chastain y a la cantante Becky G. Seguir leyendo Estilismo: Jason Rembert. Maquillaje: Jaleesa Jaikaran (Forward Artists). Peluquería: Isaac Davidson (The Only). Manicura: Gina Edwards (See Management). Producción: Cristina Serrano. Producción local: Michael Schwartz. Asistentes de fotografía: Eric Bouthiller y Morgan Goertz. Asistente digital: Dallas Raines.

items.title: ¡Felipe, Felipe!
items.description: Llevo tiempo asistiendo anonadado a la progresiva orientación del expresidente Felipe González hacia ese mundo arcaico y oscuro del que salimos en la Transición. Y una de las pruebas más evidentes es su contestación a la cariñosa sugerencia de Pepe Bono para que dejara de proclamar que iba a votar en blanco. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Los chivatos de Ayuso y la neutralidad en los institutos
items.description: Ha repartido el gobierno de Isabel Díaz Ayuso unos papelitos para denunciar a los profesores de instituto que adoctrinan. Más que denuncias, son chivatazos sin pruebas, en la mejor tradición del espionaje de visillo, más propio de un villorrio franquista que de la capital cosmopolita de la que presume la presidenta. Quiere Ayuso llenar los institutos de cotillas galdosianas, señás y tiazos que lo mismo te venden barquillos a gritos que le susurran al alguacil que te han visto repartiendo propaganda comunista. Seguir leyendo

items.title: La crisis de vivienda golpea el doble a las víctimas de violencia machista: “No quería volver a mi casa, pero no tenía dónde ir”
items.description: Lo más lejos que Carmen ha llegado a huir de su casa han sido cinco calles. Una mañana metió en la mochila de ir a trabajar algo más que la bata y las zapatillas que se ponía para limpiar: un par de mudas y un puñado de billetes que tenía escondidos. Salió como cada día como si fuese a volver cinco horas después. Llegó temblando “donde Adolfo”, el hombre al que ayudaba a bañarse y a vestirse, a hacer la compra, la comida, a quitar el polvo y a barrer y fregar el suelo, y sin poder parar de llorar le dijo: “Me quedo aquí”. Seguir leyendo

items.title: “¿Y si todo ha sido un sueño?“: la visibilidad de las mujeres en la cultura se estanca
items.description: La década posterior al impulso feminista de 2017 y 2018 trajo consigo la visibilidad de las creadoras en todas las disciplinas artísticas y, además de los focos, contribuyó a que ocuparan unos cuantos puestos de responsabilidad y liderazgo, como muestran informes de las principales asociaciones del sector y del Ministerio de Cultura. El sistema de cuotas que se estableció en industrias como la del audiovisual afianzó estas posiciones, pero como confirma Asunción Bernárdez Rodal, catedrática de Periodismo especializada en feminismo en la Universidad Complutense de Madrid, “las cifras son tercas”, porque el día a día de las mujeres de la Cultura en España a veces muestra una realidad muy distinta. Seguir leyendo

items.title: El agujero negro fiscal de España que la izquierda quiere taponar: los milmillonarios solo tributan el 0,12% de su patrimonio
items.description: La riqueza de los más acaudalados del planeta no deja de crecer y alcanza dimensiones cada vez más estratosféricas en unos sistemas fiscales que, con mil lagunas, parecen diseñados a su medida y placer. En este contexto de acumulación y de un agujero cada vez más profundo, el nivel de contribución de los multimillonarios a las arcas públicas se ha convertido en un debate cada vez más presente en los países del norte global. Las campañas electorales son un terreno propicio para poner esta cuestión sobre la mesa, y España no ha sido una excepción. Tanto el PSOE como el Frente Amplio han incluido en sus propuestas de cara al 29-N nuevos impuestos dirigidos a las mayores fortunas del país , en buena medida inspirados en las ideas del célebre economista francés Gabriel Zucman. En el debate asoma una cifra que invita a la reflexión. Y es que los multimillonarios residentes en España apenas pagan en IRPF e impuestos sobre el patrimonio una cantidad que ronda el 0,12% de toda su riqueza. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Un estudiante palestino, encarcelado sin cargos tras ser arrestado en su residencia universitaria de Jerusalén
items.description: Mahdi Tunsi —palestino de 26 años y conocido activista de izquierda en pro de la coexistencia entre judíos y árabes — estaba en la residencia estudiantil de la Universidad Hebrea de Jerusalén, donde estudia Sociología y Criminología, cuando las fuerzas de seguridad israelíes entraron y se lo llevaron arrestado. Fue hace 17 días y el estudiante sigue bajo arresto administrativo , una controvertida figura legal por la que las autoridades israelíes pueden prorrogar una detención meses (y hasta años) sin juicio ni cargos. Por eso, su vista el martes en el Tribunal de Distrito de Jerusalén fue a puerta cerrada. Y, por eso, ni él ni su abogado, Nasser Odeh, saben de qué se le acusa. “Tenía peor aspecto en esta vista”, señaló su abogado al terminar, con poco más que contar a causa del secreto de sumario. “No puedo compartir información ni con la familia”, lamentaba. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Colin Farrell y Emma Fogarty, la amistad que ha animado al actor a exponer su vida privada por una causa
items.description: “Tengo un sueño que te incluye a ti, y es hacer esta película juntos. Quiero que sea un sueño compartido”, se escucha a Colin Farrell en un audio que le manda a Emma Fogarty . Él es una reconocida estrella de Hollywood, ella, una mujer irlandesa que ha pasado toda su vida desafiando expectativas. Nació con epidermólisis ampollosa (EB), también conocida como piel de mariposa, una afección extremadamente rara y dolorosa que hace que su piel se ampolle y se desgarre con el menor contacto. Su sueño compartido es recorrer juntos los últimos cuatro kilómetros de la maratón de Dublín, un kilómetro por cada década de vida de Fogarty. Y eso que, cuando nació, los médicos dijeron a sus padres que no iba a sobrevivir una semana, y que eso era lo mejor. Un crudo recuerdo que ella misma cuenta en el documental The Slightest Touch , que se estrena este miércoles, 25 de noviembre, en HBO Max. Seguir leyendo

items.title: Cómo saber si se puede comer un alimento que ha pasado su fecha de consumo preferente
items.description: Si el orégano que tienes en el armario de la cocina todavía indica el precio en pesetas y la miel está ahí desde la primera edición de Operación Triunfo, seguramente pienses que hay alimentos que nunca se estropean y las fechas que aparecen en sus etiquetas te resultan tan extrañas como los intermitentes al conductor de un BMW. Pero debes saber que esos números no están ahí de adorno porque, aunque te parezca mentira, ni el vinagre , ni los frutos secos ni los embutidos son eternos. Si esto te pilla de sorpresa sigue leyendo, porque este artículo es para ti. items.title: Veteran actor Pete Edochie dies at 79
items.description: Veteran Nigerian actor and broadcaster Chief Pete Edochie died at 79. Edochie died at 12:30am on Wednesday, November 25, 2026, in Enugu, after a prolonged battle with prostate cancer. His death was announced in a statement signed by his son, Leo Pete Edochie, on behalf of the family and shared on Instagram on Wednesday. The statement described the deceased as a beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, adding that he hailed from Akamnato, Ifite Nteje, Anambra State. The statement read, “With profound sadness and hearts bowed in total submission to the will of Almighty God, we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, brother and kinsman, Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE, MON (Ononenyi) a retired broadcaster and veteran sctor, who departed this life on Wednesday, 25th November 2026 at 12.30am after a protracted battle with prostate cancer in Enugu, Nigeria. He was aged 79 years. “Chief Dr Pete EDOCHIE hailed from Akamnato Ifite Nteje and is survived by his beloved wife, Barrister Mrs Josephine Edochie, his children, siblings and numerous other relations. “Funeral arrangements will be announced in due course. “As we mourn this painful loss, we pray that Almighty God grants his gentle soul eternal rest and gives the entire family the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss. May God be with us all at this trying time. Amen. Chief Leo Pete EDOCHIE For the Family” Edochie was one of Nigeria’s most recognisable actors, renowned for his commanding screen presence and portrayal of traditional patriarchal figures. He rose to national and international prominence as Okonkwo in the 1987 Nigerian Television Authority adaptation of Chinua Achebe’s novel, Things Fall Apart. His performance in the television adaptation established him as a prominent figure in Nigerian acting and helped introduce his work to audiences beyond the country. Before becoming widely known as an actor, Edochie worked in broadcasting. He began working as a broadcaster in 1967 before transitioning to acting, where he built a decades-long career and appeared in numerous Nigerian films. His contributions to the entertainment industry earned him the national honour of Member of the Order of the Niger (MON).

items.title: UG, KNUST and UCC could secure new PhD programme approvals despite freeze – GTEC
items.description: The Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) has indicated that some well-established universities could still secure approval for new PhD programmes despite a nationwide freeze on new academic programmes. Deputy Director-General of GTEC, Prof. Augustine Ocloo, says institutions such as the University of Ghana (UG), Kwame Nkrumah University of Science and Technology (KNUST) and the University of Cape Coast (UCC) could be granted exemptions if they present strong justifications. Speaking on Joy News’ PM Express on Tuesday, Prof. Ocloo said the directive was not an absolute ban and that the Commission would consider exceptional cases on their individual merits. His clarification follows GTEC’s directive imposing a nationwide freeze on new programmes as part of an audit to address growing concerns over accreditation, institutional capacity and the quality of tertiary education, particularly doctoral training. “The fact that the Commission is saying to put a freeze on new Programs does not mean that if a well-established institution, for instance, UG, KNUST, UCC, should come to us with strong justification that they have to get this programme through, then the Commission will be adamant and say that okay, we have a freeze, so we’re not going to listen.” Prof. Ocloo stressed that the Commission would not rigidly enforce the directive where institutions demonstrate a compelling case. “There are human beings that work in the Commission, and they will critically analyse every situation,” he said. He explained that temporary restrictions on new programmes were not unusual in GTEC’s regulatory operations. What makes the latest intervention different is that it applies nationwide. The Deputy Director-General also apologised for the anxiety the directive may have caused within the tertiary education sector. He said the Commission had uncovered worrying cases of excessive PhD admissions at institutions without adequate capacity to train doctoral students. “For instance, you come across an institution that admits about 52 PhD students into one program. In fact, if you go all over the world, you hardly come across such matters.” He said some institutions had also failed to sustain the capacity they demonstrated when they initially secured accreditation. Prof. Ocloo assured universities that the nationwide freeze was not expected to last beyond a month. GTEC intends to deploy four or five teams to analyse data submitted by tertiary institutions and make recommendations to the Commission. However, institutions found to lack adequate capacity could face restrictions on fresh admissions for up to two years while they address their deficiencies. Existing students would not ordinarily be removed from their programmes. Prof. Ocloo maintained that the intervention was meant to protect academic standards, not undermine tertiary education. “I don’t think the commission is set out to destroy tertiary education. We are there to support and make sure that quality is sustained.”

items.title: Cifras de violaciones y pulseras antimaltrato: las medias verdades sobre violencia de género de la campaña
Delta Killings: Police summon Omo-Agege, Egbo, others for questioning
items.description: *Thugs disrupted preparations, attacked Omo-Agege’s supporters, eyewitness insists By Clifford Ndujihe, Politics Editor The police yesterday summoned former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, Ughelli North Local Government Area Chairman, Jaro Egbo and others for questioning over the political violence that erupted during a campaign rally of the Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, in Uduere community, Ughelli North LGA of Delta State on Monday. The violence has triggered fresh accusations of political intimidation, police bias and inflammatory rhetoric ahead of the 2027 general elections. While the NDC yesterday boycotted a security meeting convened by the Inspector-General of Police, IGP, Olatunji Disu, accusing the police of failing to protect its members, the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, called on President Bola Tinubu to renounce what it described as dangerous political rhetoric. On a day that supporters of the camps staged protest and counter protest over the killings in Ughelli, Delta State governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, who visited the troubled community, condemned the killings and directed security agencies to track down and arrest those responsible. The state government also imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew across Ughelli North Local Government Area. The attack occurred on Monday during a political campaign event involving former deputy president of the Senate and NDC Delta Central senatorial candidate, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege. Four persons were confirmed dead, while the NDC said no fewer than 15 others were receiving treatment in intensive care. The Inspector-General of Police subsequently ordered an immediate, impartial and evidence-based investigation, including an examination of the circumstances surrounding the shooting and the conduct of police personnel deployed to the venue. However, Vanguard gathered that one of the four supporters of Omo-Agege, killed in the attack, identified as Efemena Umukoro, had his first child barely six months ago. Yesterday, conflicting casualty figures trailed the killings. with rival political camps claiming seven deaths, against six acknowledged by Governor Sheriff Oborevwori and the police. Ughelli North Chairman, Chief Jaro Egbo, who hails from Uduere, named three persons he said were killed on his side, including the community’s President-General, PG, Cosmos Ejovwoke. Former Deputy Senate President, Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, on the other hand, listed four members of his campaign organisation died. The competing accounts bring the number of claimed fatalities to seven, although the governor and police put the toll at six, pending investigations. This was as former Chief Justice of Nigeria, Justice Olukayode Ariwoola, retd., warned against a repeat of the deadly violence that followed the 2011 general elections, which claimed over 800 lives, urging political parties, security agencies and other stakeholders to take urgent steps to protect the 2027 electoral process. Also, 53 days to the presidential and National Assembly elections of January 16, 2027, the Kimpact Development Initiative, KDI, warned that the country was sliding towards violence, disclosing that its monitoring recorded 124 incidents of electoral violence, and 22 deaths across 35 states and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Abuja between July 1 and November 23, 2026. NDC boycotts IGP’s meeting The NDC, in a statement by its National Publicity Secretary, Osa Director, said it would not attend the meeting summoned by the IGP for chairmen and secretaries of registered political parties to address attacks on campaign rallies, destruction of campaign materials and threats to public peace. The party said it no longer felt protected by the police, accusing the force of watching helplessly while its members were attacked and killed. It called on the international community to compel President Tinubu and the All Progressives Congress, APC-led government to adhere to internationally accepted democratic standards. The statement read: “The Nigeria Democratic Congress, NDC, condemns in the strongest terms the spate of violence orchestrated against its members across the country. “Therefore, the NDC has decided to boycott the security meeting called by the Inspector General of Police. We no longer feel safe and protected by a Police Force that watches helplessly the slaughter of our members across the country by hired thugs of the ruling APC. We will not lend legitimacy to a process that has failed to protect us. “The violence against NDC members has become an intolerable pattern across the length and breadth of Nigeria. “From Benue State, where our Presidential Candidate, Mr. Peter Obi, was prevented from entering the state by thugs loyal to the APC government, to Edo, Calabar, Enugu and the incessant attacks on our members in Delta State, the political temperature is on the rise, with campaigns turned into a battlefield. “Politics and campaigns are not supposed to be war. However, the APC government has turned the campaign into a battlefield, where lives have become nasty, brutish and uncertain. “The situation is compounded by the complicity of the police and security forces. The killing of four members of the NDC in Delta State was done in the full glare of the Police and security forces who were supposed to protect all Nigerians. Currently, the Nigeria Police has become an APC police sustained by taxpayers’ money. “The NDC and its members no longer feel safe and protected by the Police and security agencies, due to the manifest bias shown by their inability to carry out a proper investigation and make those responsible for the violence face the full wrath of the law.” Oborevwori orders arrest Governor Oborevwori, who visited Uduere, yesterday, to assess the situation and reassure residents, directed security agencies to identify and arrest all those involved in the killings. He had earlier held a security meeting with heads of security agencies at the Area Command Office in Ughelli. Those who accompanied him to the community included Commissioner of Police, CP Samuel Etaifo Erale; Commander, 63 Brigade of the Nigerian Army, Brigadier-General Ibrahim Buhari; the State Director of the Department of State Services, DSS, and other security officials. The governor described the killings as unfortunate and unacceptable, insisting that no political disagreement or ambition justified the loss of human lives. Warning that political activities must not become a source of insecurity, he said: “This must stop. It must stop. We cannot continue like this.” Oborevwori appealed to political leaders, supporters and other stakeholders to exercise restraint and shun political thuggery, stressing that peace and security were essential for economic growth and investment. He also directed the police and other security agencies to conduct a comprehensive investigation and ensure that all perpetrators were brought to justice. IGP orders impartial investigation In response, IGP Disu directed Delta State commissioner of police to immediately commence a thorough, impartial and evidence-based investigation into the attack. The Force Public Relations Officer, CSP Aniete Iniedu, said in a statement that the investigation would establish the sequence of events, identify those responsible and examine the circumstances surrounding the shooting, including the deployment and conduct of police personnel at the venue. The police statement read: “The Nigeria Police Force strongly condemns the deadly violence that occurred on Monday, 23 November 2026, at Uduere community, Ughelli North Local Government Area of Delta State, during a political campaign event. “The Force deeply regrets the loss of lives and injuries recorded and extends its heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families, while wishing the injured a speedy recovery. “The Force is aware of varying casualty figures circulating in the public domain. An ongoing investigation will establish the verified number of casualties and determine the circumstances surrounding the incident.” The IGP warned that any police officer found to have acted negligently, unlawfully or in breach of professional standards would face disciplinary action, while those found culpable of criminal offences would be prosecuted. The police also confirmed that Delta State government had imposed a 6pm-to-6am curfew across Ughelli North until further notice. It said security deployment, intelligence-led operations, patrols and rapid-response measures had been strengthened to prevent further violence and restore normalcy. Police invite Omo-Agege, Egbo, others for questioning Meanwhile, Delta State police command has invited principal members of the Nigerian Democratic Congress, NDC, and those of All Progressives Congress, APC, in Ughelli North for questioning in order to ascertain the facts of what transpired that led to the death of over seven persons with many injured. The command in a statement by the Public Relations Officers, SP Bright Edafe, said the invitation was necessary to enable the police uncover culpability of individual actors. The statement read: “In furtherance of the ongoing investigation, the Delta State Police Command has invited the following key political actors, and other persons of interest connected with the incident, to report to the State Criminal Investigation Department, SCID, Delta State police command Headquarters, Asaba, on the dates specified against their respective names: “Senator Ovie Omo-Agege, NDC Senatorial Candidate for Delta Central Senatorial District: Thursday, 26th November 2026 at 1100hrs. “Jaro Movudu Egbo, Chairman, Ughelli North Local Government Council, Delta State: Thursday, November 26, 2026 at 1400hrs. “Gowon Egoide, Former Chairman of Uduere Quarters, Ughelli North LGA, Delta State: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 1200hrs. “Onoriode Oneya, incumbent Youth Chairman of Uduere Community, Ughelli North LGA, Delta State: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 1200hrs “Edirin Wokode Ewhubare, an associate of Gowon Egoide from Otowvodo, Ughelli North LGA, Delta State: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 1200hrs “Erukaye Egoide, Nephew of Gowon Egoide: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 1200hrs “Tony Gabon Mevowovo, an associate of Gowon Egoide: Friday, November 27, 2026, at 1200hrs “The invitations form part of ongoing investigations aimed at establishing their level of involvement in the incident.’’ “The Commissioner of Police, Delta State Command, CP Samuel E. Erale, urges all invited persons to honour the invitations as scheduled and cooperate fully with the Police while noting that the invitations are to the mentioned individuals only as the Command will not accept the presence of supporters and other persons not explicitly invited.’’ Thugs disrupted preparations, attacked Omo-Agege’s supporters – eyewitness insists Recalling how the mayhem happened, a community leader in Uduere, Chief Joshua Asah, described the visit of Senator Ovie Omo-Agege to the community as a consultation, not a campaign rally, alleging that thugs disrupted preparations before the deadly attack that claimed four lives. Asah, who spoke with Vanguard on the telephone, said he personally informed the community’s eldest man, Chief Edward Imonikugbere, about Omo-Agege’s planned visit, following which the town hall was chosen as the venue. He alleged that a prominent politician from the community opposed the meeting and rescheduled a planned event to Monday to frustrate it. According to him, some youths who went to erect canopies on Sunday evening were chased away by suspected thugs who claimed they could not use the town hall because the politician had reserved it for a party. Asah said the Omo-Agege team subsequently moved the meeting to an open compound opposite the hall. He narrated: “On Sunday evening while some youths went to set up canopies, some thugs came and chased them away, claiming they could not use the community hall because a top politician from the town had forbidden it. “The Omo-Agege team came and had their consultation, just when Omo-Agege was about to round off his speech, the people in the community town hall started throwing stones at the crowd. There were police around but they did nothing. Before we knew it, we started hearing gunshots from them and everyone started running.” He said he escaped through the bush to neighbouring Saniko community before being rescued by his cousin. “I later heard of the killings. You can call the eldest man to confirm. It was not a campaign visit but community consultation,” he added. Efforts by Vanguard to reach Imonikugbere for confirmation were unsuccessful as his four telephone lines were switched off. Victim’s brother demands justice Meanwhile, Godwin Anaughe, elder brother of one of the victims, Moses Anaughe, expressed grief over the loss, saying the family wanted justice. “What more should I say? I have lost my brother. We want justice; his spirit will haunt those who killed him in cold blood,” he said. NDC accuses LG chairman, denies arming supporters Delta State chapter of NDC, however, accused a prominent APC politician in the area of involvement in the attack and questioned the failure of police operatives to protect its members. The party also denied allegations that its supporters were armed for self-defence, insisting that it remained committed to peaceful political engagement. Speaking on Channels Television, Delta State NDC Chairman, Anagiamaowei Oyindoubra, and Deputy Spokesperson of the NDC Presidential Campaign Council, Sam Omale, described the incident as an attack on peaceful political activities. Oyindoubra, who said he was in Asaba when the attack occurred, alleged, based on eyewitness accounts, that the politician was involved, and challenged him to produce evidence of any APC members killed or injured in the incident. He said: “The police are eyewitnesses because they were officially invited and they were there. There was no violence before the attack. If at all their persons were also injured or killed, let them produce those corpses as evidence. This is not about blackmail. We should not politicise the lives of Nigerians. We should not politicise them.” The politician in question, however, denied being at the scene, alleging that Omo-Agege’s supporters initiated the violence, which resulted in retaliation. He accused Omo-Agege and members of his entourage of instigating the violence, alleging that two of his associates, Prince Oharisi and a man identified simply as Oche, were shot dead as the former deputy Senate President and his supporters were closing their rally in Uduere. Makinde campaign accuses APC of political violence Reacting to the killing yesterday, Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation, MDPCO, accused the APC of promoting political violence to intimidate opposition parties and Nigerians ahead of the general elections. In a statement by the Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Ihediwa, stated: “This APC’s resort to killing before the 2027 general elections raises apprehension of a bigger design to use armed thugs to unleash mayhem on innocent citizens, apparently with the aim to frustrate the smooth conduct of the elections.” It recalled President Bola Tinubu’s remark to his supporters, ahead of the 2023 elections, that political power was not served in a restaurant and urged them to ‘at all cost, fight for it, grab it, snatch it and run with it.’ “This deafening silence and apparent reluctance to demand accountability deepen public apprehension and clears every doubt that the APC is not ready for a free fair, credible and peaceful democratic competition. “The resort to violence will not save the President from obvious defeat in January,” the organisation said. PDP asks Tinubu to renounce ‘war rhetoric’ Also reacting yesterday, the Kabiru Tanimu Turaki-led Interim National Working Committee, INWC, of the PDP blamed what it described as inflammatory political statements by President Tinubu for the growing climate of violence against opposition parties. In a statement by the National Publicity Secretary, Ini Ememobong, the group said the Delta attack exposed the dangers of provocative political rhetoric ahead of the 2027 elections. It demanded that Tinubu publicly renounced his past remarks, citing his 2022 declaration that political power must be “grabbed, snatched and run away with” and his 2026 remark that “all is fair in politics”. The party alleged: “These two statements alone, coming from their leader, were the adrenaline that APC followers needed to unleash unmitigated mayhem on opposition parties.’’ The PDP bloc also cited alleged threats by some APC figures, including Senator Fadahunsi of Osun State, the Chairman of Kuje Area Council and the party’s Edo State chairman, against citizens unwilling to vote for the ruling party. It alleged that intimidation of opposition figures had become recurrent in Delta, claiming that at least two deadly attacks against opposition groups occurred in November alone and were widely believed to have been sponsored by the APC. Slain supporter was six-month-old father It was learned yesterday that one of the four persons killed in the attack, identified as Efemena Umukoro, welcomed his first child barely six months earlier. Umukoro had announced the birth of his baby boy on Facebook on May 15, 2026, celebrating the safe delivery of his wife and child. In an emotional post, he described women as heroes for enduring the pains of childbirth, recounting how he stood by his wife throughout her labour. He wrote: “My Prince is here, mother and child in good health. Women are the heroes and keepers of life. “From 1cm to 10cm dilation, I stood firmly beside her through every painful minute that almost felt like a whole year suspended in time between hope and fear. “Indeed, women are heroes. They carry the deepest pains of this world in silence and strength. I watched my beautiful wife grumble and tremble in agony, entering a realm where shame no longer existed. She tore off her clothes, choosing nakedness as though in that vulnerable state she found the strength to fight a battle nature designed only for mothers. Keyamo, Okotete, Gbemre condemn killings The Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Chief Festus Keyamo, SAN, in his reaction, condemned the killings, describing the incident as alien to the Delta he knew. In a statement, titled, “This Is Not the Delta We Have Always Known”, Keyamo said he received disturbing reports of political violence in his hometown of Ughelli which left four persons dead and several others injured. He said: “I condemn in the strongest possible terms the killing of these persons, just as I also condemned the killing of a tricycle operator in broad daylight by identified supporters of a political party in Asaba on November 7, 2026.” He urged law enforcement agencies to apprehend those responsible for the killings in both Asaba and Ughelli, disclosing that he had been engaging security chiefs over the rising political violence and inflammatory rhetoric in Delta. Social crusader, Zik Gbemre, described the Uduere killings as preventable and unacceptable, insisting that no political ambition or party interest could justify the loss of lives. He also questioned the conduct of police officers allegedly present at the scene, calling on Governor Oborevwori and the Inspector-General of Police to investigate both the attackers and the officers deployed to the venue. Similarly, APC chieftain and Executive Director, Business Development, Nigerian Export-Import Bank, NEXIM, Stella Okotete, condemned the killings and demanded a thorough investigation. She said she had lost a friend, brother, confidant and political ally, Moses Anaughe, recalling that they were together last Saturday. “Moses, my peace loving dear brother, I will work with the security agencies to bring all involved in your death to book,” she said. Okotete called on the IGP, Delta State police command, National Intelligence Agency and other security agencies to establish who instigated, organised or carried out the attack and prosecute those responsible. She said the bereaved families deserved answers and regular updates on the investigation, while expressing condolences to the Anaughe family, Agbarho Kingdom and the affected political communities. Activists question police presence Also, the reported presence of dozens of security personnel at the rally has raised questions about how the violence was allowed to escalate. Lawyer and activist, Austin Nyekigbe, said he passed through Uduere on his way to Agbarha-Otor and observed a substantial security presence at the rally ground. On his return, he encountered the aftermath of the violence. He described the incident as troubling and called on the IGP to order an independent investigation into the killings and the conduct of officers deployed to the gathering. Human rights lawyer, Inibehe Effiong, also condemned the killing of Efemena Umukoro, popularly known as Akima, whom he described as a courageous rights activist. “The brutal assassination of Mr. Efemena, alias Akima, is senseless and despicable.” The fact that this dastardly killing happened in the presence of dozens of police officers is a shameful indictment of the Nigeria Police Force,’’ Effiong said. Ex-CJN warns against repeat of 2011 post-election killings Decrying the killings, former CJN Ariwoola warned against a repeat of the deadly violence that followed the 2011 general elections. Ariwoola, who is Chairman of the Council of the Wise of the Savannah Centre for Diplomacy, Democracy and Development, gave the warning at a press conference in Abuja, yesterday, expressing concern over rising political violence, intimidation, attacks on campaign convoys and destruction of property across the country. He said the trend posed a grave threat to the safety of candidates, voters, journalists and the general public, warning that failure to check it could trigger a national crisis. He said: “Recent media reports indicated that in the past five weeks, Nigeria has witnessed a disturbing recurrence of politically motivated violence and attacks in many states of the federation, thereby dangerously threatening the safety of candidates, electorates, journalists and the general public. “Since the commencement of political campaigns, reported attacks and disturbances thus far have affected political convoys of some candidates, rallies and gatherings of political parties in Kano, Katsina, Lagos, Edo, Delta, Enugu, Cross River, Sokoto, Bayelsa and Rivers states as well as the Federal Capital Territory.” The former CJN said democracy should be driven by competing ideas and policies rather than bloodshed, intimidation and coercion. Ariwoola stressed that political parties, candidates, supporters, public officials and security agencies must comply with the 1999 Constitution, the Electoral Act 2026 and relevant Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, regulations. He urged the police, Department of State Services, Nigerian Security and Civil Defence Corps, National Intelligence Agency, Defence Intelligence Agency and the Armed Forces to deploy adequate personnel to campaign venues and rallies, arrest and prosecute perpetrators, and confiscate dangerous weapons. He also tasked political party leaders and campaign councils with taking responsibility for their supporters, publicly denouncing violence, honouring the Peace Accord and sanctioning members who engage in electoral violence or threaten opponents. They were also urged to shun inflammatory, hateful and insulting statements and train campaign officials on peaceful political engagement. The council called on governments at all levels to provide a level playing field for political parties, warning against denying opposition groups access to public or private facilities for peaceful campaigns. On the role of INEC, Ariwoola said the commission must enforce electoral laws without fear or favour and work with the police to investigate and prosecute electoral offenders in accordance with Section 148 of the Electoral Act. Ariwoola said: “Political competition should be a contest of ideas, not a justification for intimidation and violence. The Council of the Wise urges all Nigerians to choose peace over violence; dialogue over threats; and democracy over anarchy. “It will be an unfortunate national shame if Nigerians collectively allow a repeat of what happened after the 2011 elections, where, according to Human Rights Watch, over 800 people were killed in the election-related violence. The 2027 elections must be won at the ballot boxes, not on the streets through intimidation and bloodshed.” 109 peace accords violated in 26 states, FCT – NPC Also, the National Peace Committee, led by former Head of State, General Abdulsalami Abubakar, retd, reported 109 violations of the peace accords in 26 states and the Federal Capital Territory during a 10-week monitoring exercise, raising fresh concerns over the conduct of political campaigns ahead of the 2027 elections. The report, covering August 19 to October 27, identified political violence and thuggery as the most frequent violations, with 33 incidents, followed by misinformation and disinformation, which accounted for 29 cases. 53 days to polls, 22 killed in 124 attacks – KDI With just 53 days to the presidential and National Assembly elections Kimpact Development Initiative, KDI, said its monitoring has recorded 124 incidents of electoral violence, and 22 deaths across 35 states and the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, Abuja between July 1 and November 23, 2026. The figures were released, yesterday, under its Nigeria Election Violence Education and Reporting, NEVER, Project. KDI said the violence escalated sharply after campaigns started – from three incidents in July, to 48 in October, and 40 in the first half of November alone. “The overall trajectory suggests that electoral competition is becoming increasingly accompanied by violence and intimidation, if left unchecked, these trends could intensify further as election day approaches.” KDI added. The violence is no longer confined to traditional hotspots. Kano, Delta, Rivers, Edo, Ondo and Kebbi recorded significant incidents, but almost the entire country is now affected. Physical assault accounted for 46.8% of cases, property destruction 28.8%, shootings 10.2%, intimidation and harassment 9%, and kidnappings 4%. KDI also flagged a dangerous rise in hostile rhetoric, threats and inflammatory statements across party lines, warning that such language normalises violence and emboldens supporters. Most damning is who is behind it. Political party members and affiliated groups were identified as perpetrators in 82.3% of incidents and as victims in 86.5%. “Political leaders must take concrete measures to discourage violence, sanction supporters who engage in unlawful conduct, and publicly demonstrate their commitment to peaceful elections,” KDI said. The group also raised alarm over growing political intolerance — restrictions on opposition activities, abuse of administrative authority, and denial of equal opportunities to campaign. Despite several arrests reported since January, KDI said it has found no publicly available evidence of corresponding prosecutions or convictions in many cases. “This accountability deficit weakens deterrence and can create the perception that perpetrators of electoral violence can act with impunity,” it said. Kingsley Omonobi, Henry Umoru, Jimitota Onoyume, Egufe Yafugborhi, John Alechenu, Juliet Umeh, Efe Onodjae, Akpokona Omafuaire, Ochuko Akuopha & Luminous Jannamike also contributed to this report. items.title: Cashless divide
items.description: IMAGINE a woman in Islamabad arriving at a government office to pay a fee. She has the money, but no bank account and no smartphone of her own. The counter no longer accepts cash. The official points her towards a QR code. She asks someone nearby to make the payment for her. The payment goes through, but she has had to depend on a stranger to make it. This is a hypothetical situation, but it captures a problem beneath the government’s plan to make Islamabad cashless by the end of December. Do people have the means to participate? And what happens to those who do not? There are good reasons to encourage digital payments. They can make transactions easier to trace, reduce delays and help bring economic activity into the formal system. Raast and other payment infrastructure can make this possible at a scale that cash cannot. But encouraging digital payments is different from withdrawing cash before people have a workable alternative. That distinction matters. The Pakistan Bureau of Statistics’ Household Integrated Economic Survey 2024-25 puts the gap in perspective. Internet use among individuals stands at 57 per cent, falling to 49pc in rural areas, compared with 69pc in urban areas. Only half the population owns a mobile phone. Ownership is 69pc among men and 39pc among women. These figures do not tell us how many people can use a banking application, but they do show how uneven access to the basic tools of a cashless economy remains. People should not be turned away from a government office because they cannot make a digital payment. The gap is even wider when we look at access to financial services. According to the World Bank’s Global Findex 2025, based on 2024 data, only 12pc of women in Pakistan have an account, compared with 42pc of men. Digital payment use stands at 13pc for women and 40pc for men. Among the poo­r­­est 40pc of adults, only 9pc made digital paym­e­nts, compared with 33pc among the wealthiest 60pc. For someone with a bank account, a smartphone and reliable internet, cashless payments may simply be more convenient. Someone paying in cash, living on an irregular income, sharing a phone or unfamiliar with digital interfaces may experience the same change as an additional expense. They may have to travel to an agent, pay a fee or ask someone else to make the transaction. They may also be unable to pay when a system is unavailable. The fact that everyone is being asked to use the same system does not mean everyone is equally able to use it. This becomes a more serious concern when the state makes digital payment the only option. From Dec 1, Islamabad’s ICT administration and CDA departments are expected to stop accepting cash. What will happen to someone who has no bank account or cannot use a digital application? Will there be assisted payment facilities? What happens during a network outage, a failed transfer or a disputed transaction? People should not be turned away from a government office because they cannot make a digital payment. Access is only part of the issue. A cashless economy also changes the information generated by ordinary transactions. A digital payment can create a record of who paid whom, how much and when. Depending on the system, it may also be linked to a location or other identifying information. Over time, these records can reveal patterns of work, movement, consumption and association. Of course, this does not mean government departments can simply access everyone’s financial records. That depends on the legal powers they have and the arrangements governing access to the information. But as more everyday activity moves onto digital payment systems, these questions become harder to ignore. Pakistan’s wider digital transformation makes this concern more immediate. Government departments are developing systems to exchange data, while digital identity and AI-assisted services are becoming part of policy discussions. Much of the promise of these systems lies in bringing information from different sources together. But that also creates the possibility of using information beyond the reason it was originally collected. Data generated to complete a payment should not become available for unrelated profiling or decision-making simply because it is technically possible to combine datasets. This raises some basic questions. Who can access transaction data, and for what purpose? How long is it kept? What safeguards apply when banks, payment providers and public bodies are involved? Can individuals find out if their information has been misused and seek a remedy? Pakistan has sectoral financial regulations and legal protections, but it still lacks an enacted, comprehensive personal data protection law. As the amount of financial information being generated grows, the absence of clear and enforceable rules becomes harder to justify. The government should measure Cashless Islamabad by more than the number of merchants displaying QR codes. It needs to establish who is being left out and provide assisted, low-cost ways to pay. Cash or another accessible alternative should remain available where digital access cannot reasonably be assumed, particularly for essential public services. A policy deadline cannot substitute for evidence that these arrangements actually work. There should also be clear procedures for failed transactions, refunds and complaints. Access to payment data must be limited by law and purpose, with proper audit trails and independent oversight. Moving towards digital payments may help document economic activity and make transactions easier. But before making cash unavailable, the government needs to ask a more basic question: can people actually use the alternatives being offered to them? The state is changing more than the way citizens pay. It is changing the conditions on which they participate in public and economic life. That change should make participation easier, not leave people behind because of their income, gender, location or access to technology. The writer is a technology lawyer specialising in data protection. Published in Dawn, November 25th, 2026

items.title: ONU : près de 47.000 femmes et filles tuées par un proche en 2025
items.description: L'Office des Nations Unies contre la drogue et le crime (ONUDC) et ONU Femmes ont indiqué que quelque 47.000 femmes et filles ont été tuées intentionnellement en 2025 par un membre de leur famille ou par un partenaire intime, soit une moyenne de cinq victimes par heure. Selon de nouvelles données publiées mardi à l’occasion de la Journée internationale pour l’élimination de la violence à l’égard des femmes, célébrée le 25 novembre, le domicile demeure le lieu le plus dangereux pour les femmes et les filles. Sur les quelque 78.000 féminicides recensés dans le monde en 2025, 60% ont été commis par un partenaire intime ou un proche, révèle le rapport. L’Afrique affiche le taux le plus élevé de féminicides commis dans la sphère familiale, avec 2,9 victimes pour 100.000 femmes, devant les Amériques (1,4), l’Océanie (1,1), l’Asie (0,6) et l’Europe (0,5). Citée dans le rapport, la directrice exécutive de l’ONUDC, Monica Juma, a appelé à renforcer les stratégies de prévention et les dispositifs de protection, alors que la cheffe d’ONU Femmes, Sima Bahous, a insisté sur la nécessité de garantir aux victimes un accès sûr aux mécanismes de signalement et de protection. Le rapport relève, par ailleurs, que les taux de féminicides diminuent beaucoup plus lentement que ceux des homicides en général. Selon les auteurs, la baisse apparente du nombre de victimes par rapport à 2024 s’explique principalement par l’amélioration des données disponibles et ne traduit pas un recul réel du phénomène.
